proof.text: Extract the coordinate equation, naturality and unique mapping property of the chosen relative lift from lem-zl-component-relative-profinite-site. Continuous maps into a profinite pullback are constructed through its standard subspace homeomorphism. For f:Y→X, send a point of the scheme pullback to (the E-coordinate of its X-lift projection, the component of its Y-projection). The pullback equation and naturality of connected components make this a continuous coordinate over Y. The mapping property gives the forward comparison. Conversely, the E-coordinate of the Y-lift gives a unique map to the X-lift over X; pair it with the Y structure map using the scheme pullback property.

Maps into a relative lift are equal when they have the same structure morphism and continuous coordinate, by uniqueness in its mapping property. In a profinite pullback equality follows from both projections. Apply these facts to the two comparison composites; for the scheme pullback also use pullback.hom_ext. This gives inverse maps. Apply the same uniqueness to the transition maps for any E→E′ to obtain a natural isomorphism.

The connected-component map preserves identity and composition, as checked on representatives. For the identity choose the slice isomorphism whose underlying map is the first pullback projection. For composition choose the standard pullback-pasting isomorphism after rewriting the component map. The first and second projections give the stated equations. To check the comparison coherence, use uniqueness into the relative Z-lift and then both projections of each profinite pullback. Their E projections agree by comparison-coordinate naturality and the first-projection equation of Over.pullbackComp; the remaining projections agree by the Over structure equations. The latter first-projection equation follows from the counit equation for conjugate adjunctions.

Use the geometric relative-lift description for the chosen X-lift. For the finite stage X-components indexed by a, send each actual restricted open into the lift by the unique mapping property with coordinate (component(x),a). Its image is exactly finite-label fibre a: the pullback homeomorphism proves both inclusions. The map is an embedding because its composite to X is the restricted open inclusion; its range is open and its stalk maps are isomorphisms by cancellation against those of the structure map. Thus these are disjoint open immersions covering the lift, so form a coproduct. Pullback of each open immersion is an open immersion; the open-fibre-product range formula identifies its range with the inverse image of that label fibre. Compose with the comparison isomorphism. Its coordinate formula identifies the resulting range with label-a points of the Y-lift. The structure equation forces these points to lie over the specified Y-open, giving precisely the intersection in the statement, including repeated labels and empty fibres. These transported disjoint open immersions again cover, giving the required Y-coproduct.

For any permitted presentation, the X-relative-lift theorem makes its image a limit cone. The slice scheme pullback is a right adjoint and preserves this limit. Transport the resulting limiting cone through the comparison natural isomorphism to obtain the other limit cone. Each cone equation is the naturality equation of that same isomorphism. No assertion that base change preserves the chosen finite-stage syntax is required.

title: Affine relative component lifts commute with arbitrary affine base change
statement:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Put $P=\pi_0(X)$, $Q=\pi_0(Y)$ with their quotient topologies and $h=\pi_0(f):Q\to P$ [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite]. Work in the compatible universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For each profinite space $E\to P$, let $X_E=X\times_P E$ be the affine relative component lift, defined by the inverse limit of its finite clopen stages [lem-zl-component-relative-profinite-site]; for a profinite $Q$-space $F$ let $Y_F$ be the analogous lift. Then there are canonical isomorphisms of $Y$-schemes
$$c_{f,E}:Y\times_X X_E\xrightarrow{\sim}Y_{Q\times_P E},$$
where the left side is a scheme fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] and $Q\times_P E$ is the topological fibre product of profinite spaces. They preserve the projections to $Y$ and $E$, are natural in $E\to P$, and agree with the associativity identifications for identity and composite affine morphisms $f$. On a finite clopen stage they identify the pullback of each open-and-closed part $X_U$ with $Y_{h^{-1}U}$; they commute with the limiting cones of every cofiltered finite-stage presentation. In particular, the two functors from profinite $P$-spaces to $Y$-schemes, $E\mapsto Y\times_X X_E$ and $E\mapsto Y_{Q\times_P E}$, are naturally isomorphic with these normalizations. No henselian, w-local, w-contractible, surjectivity or nonemptiness hypothesis is imposed.
